description: Learning cards with subtitle, body paragraphs, and takeaway per card.

cards.title: The Universe Doesn't Need a Beginning
cards.subtitle: What happened before the Big Bang? The question itself might be broken.
body: Hawking said time could be like a sphere—finite but boundless. No first moment. No 'before.'
Asking what's north of the North Pole makes the same mistake.
cards.takeaway: Some questions are malformed, not unanswered.

cards.title: There's No Universal Now
cards.subtitle: Your GPS would be off by miles if engineers hadn't corrected for time running differently in orbit.
body: Satellites tick faster than ground clocks. Gravity slows time. An astronaut near light speed ages slower than her twin.
Simultaneity depends on where you're standing and how fast you're moving.
cards.takeaway: Time is local, not universal.

cards.title: Gravity Is Geometry
cards.subtitle: The sun doesn't pull you. It bends space, and you fall through the curve.
body: Newton called gravity a force. Einstein called it geometry.
Earth doesn't orbit because it's pulled—it follows the straightest path through curved spacetime.
cards.takeaway: Mass tells space how to curve. Space tells mass how to move.

cards.title: Black Holes Break Physics
cards.subtitle: Cross the event horizon and escape requires moving faster than light.
body: We've photographed a black hole (M87, 2019). What's at the center remains unknown.
The equations predict infinite density and break down. Singularities mean we need a deeper theory.
cards.takeaway: General relativity admits its own failure at singularities.

cards.title: The Uncertainty Principle Is Fundamental
cards.subtitle: Better instruments won't help. Nature forbids knowing both position and momentum precisely.
body: The electron doesn't have a location before measurement. It has probabilities.
This isn't a bug—it's a feature of reality.
cards.takeaway: The universe at its smallest is fundamentally fuzzy.

cards.title: Light Speed Is the Limit
cards.subtitle: Approach it and time dilates, mass increases, length contracts.
body: The speed of light is the maximum for information, energy, matter.
Reach it and time stops entirely. Particle accelerators confirm this.
cards.takeaway: Every theory in modern physics respects this limit or fails.

cards.title: The Big Bang Wasn't an Explosion Into Space
cards.subtitle: Space itself was born and started stretching. There was no 'outside.'
body: Every point in the universe was the same point 13.8 billion years ago.
Galaxies aren't flying apart—the fabric between them is stretching.
cards.takeaway: Space and time started together—there is no 'outside.'

cards.title: Space Expands Faster Than Light
cards.subtitle: Distant galaxies recede faster than light. Space itself has no speed limit.
body: The expansion is accelerating, driven by dark energy we don't understand.
Some galaxies have already crossed our cosmic horizon. We'll never see them.
cards.takeaway: Objects can't exceed light speed, but space itself can.

cards.title: Black Holes Evaporate
cards.subtitle: Hawking proved they leak energy and eventually disappear.
body: Quantum particle pairs near the event horizon—one falls in, one escapes.
This raises the information paradox: what happens to everything that fell in?
cards.takeaway: The paradox remains unsolved.

cards.title: The Arrow of Time Is Statistical
cards.subtitle: Physics equations work forward and backward. Entropy picks the direction.
body: A broken egg could reassemble—physics allows it—but the odds are astronomically small.
The second law of thermodynamics creates the arrow we experience.
cards.takeaway: The arrow of time is probability, not law.

cards.title: Relativity and Quantum Don't Talk
cards.subtitle: Both work perfectly. Apply both at once and the math explodes.
body: Inside a black hole, at the Big Bang—the equations break.
String theory and loop quantum gravity are candidates. Neither proven.
cards.takeaway: The gap is the deepest unsolved problem in physics.

cards.title: Observation Collapses the Wave Function
cards.subtitle: The electron is a wave until you measure it. Then it's a particle.
body: Particles exist in superposition until measured. Not metaphor—experimentally confirmed.
The double-slit experiment: electrons act as waves until observed.
cards.takeaway: Measurement changes reality.

cards.title: Entropy Always Wins
cards.subtitle: The star burns out. The ice melts. Order doesn't hold.
body: Every pocket of order is temporary, fighting an inevitable tide.
Heat death: a universe at maximum entropy, no energy differences left.
cards.takeaway: Order is expensive, temporary, and borrowed.

cards.title: 95% of the Universe Is Unknown
cards.subtitle: Dark matter and dark energy. We named the gaps.
body:
• Galaxies spin too fast for visible matter
• Dark energy accelerates expansion
• We can't see or explain either
95% of the universe is made of things we don't understand.
cards.takeaway: We named the gaps and kept calculating.

cards.title: Quantum Entanglement Is Real
cards.subtitle: Measure one particle; instantly a particle light-years away changes state.
body: Einstein called it 'spooky action at a distance' and hated it.
Bell's theorem proved it: the universe is fundamentally non-local.
cards.takeaway: Particles that interacted once remain connected.

cards.title: We Hear Gravitational Waves
cards.subtitle: Two black holes collided 1.3 billion years ago. LIGO detected the ripple in 2015.
body: Einstein predicted waves in spacetime. He thought they'd be too weak to detect.
We can now observe the universe through spacetime ripples, not just light.
cards.takeaway: We're listening to collisions from billions of years ago.

cards.title: The Higgs Completes the Standard Model
cards.subtitle: Particles shouldn't have mass. CERN found the field that gives it to them.
body: Photons don't interact with the Higgs field—massless. Electrons do—mass.
The Standard Model is complete but doesn't include gravity or dark matter.
cards.takeaway: It's the best incomplete theory we have.

cards.title: The Anthropic Principle
cards.subtitle: The constants are tuned for life. 'If they weren't, we wouldn't exist to ask.'
body: Change gravity slightly and stars don't form. The constants seem finely tuned.
Some invoke the multiverse: infinite universes, we're in one that permits life.
cards.takeaway: Either profound or circular, depending on who you ask.

cards.title: Progress Happens Where Theories Break
cards.subtitle: Newton broke Aristotle. Einstein broke Newton.
body: Science replaces incomplete theories with more complete ones.
Relativity and quantum both work—except where they overlap. That's the frontier.
cards.takeaway: Better theories reveal limits, not destroy predecessors.

cards.title: We Are Insignificant, and We Figured It Out
cards.subtitle: Small planet. Average star. One galaxy among trillions.
body: We've measured the cosmic microwave background, detected gravitational waves, photographed a black hole.
Ants on a speck figured out the age and fate of the cosmos.
cards.takeaway: The audacity is the point.
